title: Refunds Returning to Gift Cards & Store Credit Instruments
content:
Value refunded on an order or a return goes back to the Gift Cards & Store Credit instrument it was spent from, up to the amount spent from that instrument on that order. It never goes to a different instrument, to a card or to cash.

## Where the refund lands, by the instrument's state

A refund is loaded onto the instrument only while it is in status active, depleted or locked. The state is read from the instrument's record in the system.

| State of the instrument the value was spent from | What happens to the refund |
|---|---|
| Active | Loaded onto the instrument |
| Depleted | Loaded onto the instrument, which becomes active again |
| Locked | Loaded onto the instrument and kept frozen with its protected balance |
| Closed by replacement or by consolidation | Follows the balance to the instrument recorded as counterpart on its transfer-out entry |
| Expired, Marlowe Rewards Note | A new Marlowe Rewards Note is issued for the refunded value under the Marlowe Rewards reissue rule for refunds on returns |
| Expired, Bonus Gift Card or Goodwill Credit | The refunded value is forfeited and not paid to any other tender |

Only one refund entry is loaded per instrument, order, return and refund date.

## Illustrations (hypothetical figures)

- An order was paid 40.00 from a Marlowe & Finch e-Gift Card and 60.00 by card. A full refund returns 40.00 to that e-Gift Card, and no more than 40.00, because the refund to the instrument is limited to what was spent from it on that order.
- A Return Store Credit spent down to 0.00 is depleted. A 15.00 refund on an order it paid is loaded onto it, and the credit is active again with a balance of 15.00.
- A Goodwill Credit that paid part of an order has expired by the time the order is refunded. The refunded part is forfeited; it is not paid back by card or to any other instrument.
- A refund for the same instrument, order and return already loaded on a given refund date is not loaded a second time for that date.
